introduction: This spec gives each of the four agent-fox tools (spec, issue, fix, impl) a --schema flag that prints, without doing any work, a single JSON document describing the flags it accepts and the JSON Schema of what it returns, and adds a schema_version field to the ordinary envelope so a caller can tell which shape of the shared interface it is looking at.

glossary.JSON Schema 2020-12: The JSON Schema meta-schema draft this feature's flags and result documents are written against and validated with.
glossary.envelope: The single JSON object (toolio.Envelope) every agent-fox tool writes to stdout on an ordinary run.
glossary.flags document: The self-description document's flags value: a standalone JSON Schema 2020-12 document describing the tool's flag set.
glossary.golden file: A checked-in file holding the exact bytes a command is expected to produce, compared byte-for-byte by a test.
glossary.result document: The self-description document's result value: a standalone JSON Schema 2020-12 document describing the envelope shape that tool actually writes, with its own Result type substituted in.
glossary.self-description document: The single JSON object a tool prints instead of running, when invoked with --schema.

requirements.title: The --schema flag: precedence and isolation from a run
requirements.rationale: A caller has to be able to ask what a tool accepts and returns without risking a network call, a credential check, or a change to the repository.

criteria.action: register a boolean --schema flag with default false, alongside the existing shared flags

criteria.condition: a tool is invoked with --schema set to true and --version is not set
criteria.action: build the tool's self-description document and write it to stdout as indented JSON followed by a newline
criteria.contract: the process exits 0; stdout contains exactly one JSON object followed by a trailing newline and nothing else

criteria.condition: a tool is invoked with both --schema and --version set
criteria.action: honor --version's existing precedence by printing the build identity line and exiting, without printing the self-description document
take no run-related action for any of those flags: create no output file, no events sink, and no run
criteria.contract: no file exists at any path named by --output, --events or --events-file after the process exits; stdout carries only the self-description document

criteria.condition: --schema is given together with a positional argument
criteria.action: accept the positional argument and ignore it, producing output identical to the same invocation without it
criteria.contract: the stdout bytes for '<tool> --schema "some text"' equal the stdout bytes for '<tool> --schema'

criteria.condition: another flag given alongside --schema fails flag.Parse's own validation, such as an unknown flag or a malformed value
criteria.action: report flag.Parse's existing error and not print the self-description document
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stderr carries the flag package's own parse error; stdout does not contain the self-description document's tool or flags keys

criteria.condition: a tool is invoked with --schema, no environment variable naming a model credential set, and --dir pointing at an existing empty directory
criteria.action: exit 0 printing the document, making no network call, requiring no repository at --dir, and resolving no model
criteria.contract: exit code 0; the document is printed; no outbound network connection is made; no credential or model-resolution error is raised

requirements.title: The self-description document's shape
requirements.rationale: A caller needs one document per tool that names what it does, what it takes, and how it can end, without reading Go source or docs/cli.md.

criteria.action: carry exactly the top-level keys tool, schema_version, description, input, flags, result, and exit_codes
carry, in its tool and schema_version fields, the same values Envelope.Tool and Envelope.SchemaVersion carry on an ordinary run of that tool
carry, in its description field, the tool's own hand-authored one-sentence App.Description value, set once in that tool's cmd/<tool>/main.go

carry an input field shaped {"description": string, "kinds": ["text", "file", "stdin", "issue"]}, whose description is the tool's hand-authored App.InputDescription value and whose kinds is always this same four-element list regardless of which kinds that tool's own CheckInput accepts

carry an exit_codes field whose keys are exactly the exit codes that tool's Exec can return under App's shared exit table, each paired with a one-line hand-authored description from that tool's App.ExitCodes
for issue and spec, carry an exit_codes field with exactly the three keys "0", "1", and "2"
for fix and impl, carry an exit_codes field with exactly the five keys "0", "1", "2", "3", and "4"

requirements.title: flags, generated from the tool's FlagSet
requirements.rationale: A hand-written flags document drifts from the FlagSet the moment one changes and the other does not, so it has to be derived.

criteria.action: build the flags document by walking flag.FlagSet.VisitAll over the fully-populated FlagSet App.Main constructs, Common's registration followed by the tool's own Flags closure, in the name order VisitAll visits

criteria.condition: a registered flag is named schema or version
criteria.action: exclude that flag from the flags document's properties
criteria.contract: flags.properties has no key named 'schema' and no key named 'version'

criteria.action: for every other registered flag, set that property's description to the flag's Usage string verbatim

criteria.guard: Get() returns a dynamic type of string, bool, int64, or float64
criteria.action: set that property's type to the matching JSON Schema primitive ("string", "boolean", or "integer"/"number") and its default to the flag's own default value
set that property's schema to {"type": "string", "format": "duration"}, with default rendered as the duration's own string form, for example "10m0s"

criteria.condition: a flag's Value does not implement flag.Getter, such as fix's hand-written --pull flag
criteria.action: report that property as {"type": "string"}, with default taken from the flag's own String method
criteria.contract: flags.properties['pull'] equals {"type": "string", "default": <the flag's String() result>, "description": <the flag's Usage>}

criteria.condition: a flag has been declared, as part of this scope's implementation, to carry a closed set of legal values, such as --land on fix and impl and any flag from an earlier scope of this split that has one
criteria.action: include an enum key on that flag's property listing exactly that declared set
produce the flags document shaped {"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "type": "object", "properties": {...}}, with no required key and no additionalProperties key

requirements.title: result, generated from Go types by reflection
requirements.rationale: A caller's own tooling needs the real shape of what a tool returns, derived from the Go types that actually get marshalled rather than hand-maintained separately.

criteria.action: render a Go struct type as {"type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...]}, with property order following reflect.VisibleFields' declaration order, including fields promoted from an anonymously embedded struct

derive a field's JSON property name and required-ness from its json struct tag exactly as encoding/json reads it: a tag carrying omitempty removes the field from required, a tag's absence keeps the field in required, and a field tagged json:"-" is skipped entirely

render a slice field as {"type": "array", "items": <element schema>}, a pointer field as its pointee's own schema without a separate nullable marker, and a scalar field as the matching JSON Schema primitive type
for any field reachable from toolio.Envelope or from one of the four tools' Result types, set that field's schema description from a new struct tag read alongside json
serialize an object schema's properties as an ordered sequence through a custom MarshalJSON, never as a plain Go map, so property order is preserved regardless of encoding/json's own map-key sorting

criteria.condition: the result document for a specific tool is built
criteria.action: apply itself to toolio.Envelope and substitute the schema of that tool's own concrete Result type, taken from a zero-value App.ResultSample, for the Envelope.Result field's schema
criteria.contract: result.properties.result equals the object schema generated from that tool's own Result struct, not a generic {"type": "object"} placeholder

criteria.action: produce a result document shaped {"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...]}, valid as a standalone JSON Schema document independent of the flags document

requirements.title: schema_version on the envelope, and the additive/breaking rule it names
requirements.rationale: A caller needs to tell a shape it understands from one it does not before it acts on an envelope, separate from the build identity.

criteria.action: carry a SchemaVersion string field, tagged json:"schema_version", positioned immediately after Version in field order, present on every ordinary envelope without an omitempty tag
define one package-level constant SchemaVersion that all four tools use to set Envelope.SchemaVersion, so all four always advertise the same value
set the SchemaVersion constant to "2.0.0"
carry the same schema_version value under the same key, as a new field on the already-closed event type

classify as additive, not requiring a major version bump, each of: a new top-level envelope field, a new field on an existing object such as result, needs_human, error, a warning, or an event, a new value in a field whose own description documents it as an open set, and a new event type
classify as breaking, requiring a major version bump, each of: removing or renaming a field, changing a field's type, and narrowing a field documented as a closed enum

requirements.title: A golden-file test per tool, and an exhaustiveness check on descriptions
requirements.rationale: Nothing keeps a generated document honest except a test that fails the moment the source it is generated from moves and the checked-in document does not.

criteria.action: keep one checked-in golden file cmd/<tool>/testdata/schema.golden.json per tool, holding the exact bytes that tool's --schema output produces

criteria.condition: a change to a field reachable from a tool's Result type, to a flag's type, default, or declared enum, or to the envelope's own shape is made without updating that tool's checked-in golden file
criteria.action: fail, reporting a byte-level diff between the built tool's live --schema output and the checked-in golden file
criteria.contract: make test exits non-zero and its output names the tool and shows the diff between the live and golden bytes

criteria.condition: the golden-file update path, an environment variable or test flag, is given
criteria.action: regenerate the golden file from the live --schema output instead of failing
compile both the flags document and the result document of every tool's --schema output against the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema, using github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6
criteria.contract: the test fails, naming the tool and which document (flags or result) did not compile, when either does not compile against the meta-schema

criteria.action: walk, by reflection, every field reachable from toolio.Envelope and from each of the four tools' Result types, and fail naming any field lacking the description struct tag 09-REQ-4 requires
criteria.contract: the test fails and its failure message lists every field missing the description tag

requirements.title: Documentation: docs/cli.md and the envelope-versioning ADR
requirements.rationale: The compatibility rule only protects a caller if it is written down once, in a place every future change to the envelope is expected to consult and extend.

criteria.action: contain a --schema row in the shared-flags table describing its default and its effect
contain a Self-description (--schema) section with one abbreviated worked example and an explanation of the flags, result, and exit_codes keys
contain an Interface versions section listing 1.0.0 and 2.0.0, one paragraph each, stating the additive/breaking rule from 09-REQ-5, and serving as the place a future major bump appends its own entry

contain a new ADR file docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md recording, as an accepted decision, the context, the semver additive-only decision with its closed additive/breaking list, and the consequence that a future spec touching the envelope states which kind of change it makes

execution_paths.title: A caller introspects a tool's interface before ever running it

steps.action: invokes 'fix --schema' with no model credential configured and --dir pointing at an empty directory
parses flags, detects --schema, and builds the self-description document without resolving a model, checking a credential, or touching the network
writes the document as indented JSON to stdout and exits 0
compiles the document's flags and result values against the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema and reads exit_codes to plan how to call fix

execution_paths.title: A maintainer changes a Result field and the golden-file test catches the drift

steps.action: adds a new field to codefix.Result without updating cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json
builds fix, runs 'fix --schema', and compares the live output byte-for-byte against the checked-in golden file
fails, printing a diff between the live document and the golden file
regenerates the golden file through the update path and reruns make test until it passes

execution_paths.title: An ordinary run reports the same interface version its own --schema advertised

steps.action: invokes 'issue' with a valid report as input, with no --schema flag
completes the run and calls Run.Envelope, which sets schema_version to the shared toolio.SchemaVersion constant ("2.0.0") alongside version
writes the ordinary envelope, including schema_version, to stdout
compares the envelope's schema_version against the value 'issue --schema' advertised earlier and proceeds only when they match
